confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer figures come from my searches of aggregated cost-of-living data. Numbeo's October 2026 Split figures were about EUR 15 for an inexpensive meal, EUR 66 for a mid-range dinner for two, EUR 2.48 for a cappuccino and EUR 4.25 for a domestic draft beer. Wise, Expatistan and Bookiscout gave figures in a similar range. I raised these slightly for the July 2026 peak season and for prices in the tourist core. Cocktail and wine figures come from searched nightlife and travel guides that only gave ranges, about EUR 9-15 for a cocktail and EUR 5-8 for a glass of wine. Some of those guides looked generic or out of date, so these two anchors are less certain. I converted euros to US dollars using my own estimate of about 1.16 USD per EUR, not a looked-up rate. All four accommodation anchors are my own judgement based on general knowledge, not on any booking listings. Split's July prices are among the highest of the year, so the hostel and hotel figures are the least certain and could vary by plus or minus 25-35 percent.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Numbeo, Expatistan and Wise data for Split itself for food and drink. For accommodation, I compared Split with peak-season Dubrovnik (somewhat more expensive) and other Adriatic and Mediterranean beach cities like Zadar and Kotor, where July demand pushes hostel and hotel rates well above the yearly average.
